name: papr_hvpipe_dev_create_handle
prose: Opens a handle for HVPIPE source srcID and returns a file descriptor or a negative errno. The local src_info is declared with __free(kfree). It takes hvpipe_src_list_lock and calls hvpipe_find_source(srcID); if a source is found it releases the lock, logs the owning task pid and returns -EALREADY (on this return src_info still holds the pointer to the found entry, and the __free(kfree) cleanup runs on it at scope exit). Otherwise it unlocks and allocates a zeroed hvpipe_source_info with kzalloc(GFP_KERNEL_ACCOUNT), returning -ENOMEM on failure, sets srcID and tsk = current, initialises recv_wqh, and prepares an fd and an anon-inode file (anon_inode_getfile with papr_hvpipe_handle_ops and src_info as private_data) via FD_PREPARE; if that fails it returns fdf.err and src_info is freed by the cleanup. On success it calls retain_and_null_ptr(src_info) so the file owns the allocation, retakes the lock and checks hvpipe_find_source(srcID) again; if another source with that ID now exists it unlocks and returns -EALREADY (the prepared file is then released by the FD_PREPARE cleanup; the release handler papr_hvpipe_handle_release does list_del on src_info->list and kfree, although the entry was not added to the list on this path). Otherwise it adds src_info to hvpipe_src_list, unlocks, and returns fd_publish(fdf), the installed file descriptor number (nonnegative; fd_publish has no failure return).
note: Reviewer 1 (success returns fd not 0) right, stated. Reviewer 2 (source remains on list if fd_publish fails) WRONG: fd_publish (include/linux/file.h:224-233) only installs the fd and cannot fail, and the list_add at papr-hvpipe.c:530 precedes it. Reviewer 3 (FD_PREPARE cleanup fputs the file so release list_dels) concerns the second -EALREADY path and is right about the cleanup (release at papr-hvpipe.c:459-475). Slice cut head; real function at 486-533. Possible latent bug noted (not fixed): kfree of the found entry via __free on the first -EALREADY return.

name: pmem_drc_add_node
prose: Adds the persistent-memory node for DRC index drc_index. It calls dlpar_acquire_drc; if that fails it logs and returns -EINVAL with nothing held. It then calls dlpar_configure_connector(cpu_to_be32(drc_index), pmem_node); if that returns NULL it calls dlpar_release_drc(drc_index) and returns -EINVAL. It then calls dlpar_attach_node(dn, pmem_node); if that returns a nonzero rc it logs, calls dlpar_release_drc(drc_index), calls dlpar_free_cc_nodes(dn) only if that release call returns nonzero, and returns rc. On success it logs and returns 0; the new node is attached under pmem_node (a platform device is created by the of reconfig notifier).
note: Reviewer (connector nodes freed only when DRC release fails on attach failure) RIGHT, stated (pmem.c:56-57); contract removed (weak/vacuous, ssize_t return). Slice cut head; real function at 29-65.

name: recover_mce
prose: Decides whether a machine check can be treated as recovered; returns 1 or 0. It starts with recovered = 0. If regs_is_unrecoverable(regs) (MSR_RI clear) it logs and leaves recovered at 0; else if evt->disposition is MCE_DISPOSITION_RECOVERED it sets recovered = 1; else if evt->severity is MCE_SEV_FATAL it logs and leaves recovered at 0 (any other case also leaves it 0). Then, only if recovered is 0 and evt->sync_error is set: if the interrupt came from user mode it calls _exception(SIGBUS, regs, BUS_MCEERR_AR, regs->nip) and sets recovered = 1; else if die_will_crash() is true it leaves recovered at 0; else it calls die_mce("Machine check", regs, SIGBUS) (which may not return) and sets recovered = 1. It returns recovered. So an unrecoverable (RI clear) or fatal event can still return 1 when sync_error is set and the interrupt came from user mode or die_will_crash() is false.
note: Reviewers 2 and 3 (RI-clear/unrecoverable does not always return 0; sync_error path can return 1) RIGHT: ras.c:799-825. Reviewer 1 (omits return 0 cases) addressed. Slice cut head; real function at 782-828.

name: hcall_return_busy_check
prose: Takes a pseries hcall return code rc and returns it, possibly converted. If H_IS_LONG_BUSY(rc) is true it computes ms = clamp(get_longbusy_msecs(rc), 1, 10), sleeps with usleep_range(ms * 100 us, ms * 1000 us), sets rc to H_BUSY (1) and returns it. Else if rc == H_BUSY it calls cond_resched() and returns rc (1). For any other value it returns rc unchanged with no sleep or yield.
note: Reviewer 1 (H_BUSY is 1) right, prose says H_BUSY (1). Reviewer 15 (sleep is 0.1*ms to ms, not 1-10 ms) RIGHT: vas.c:61 usleep_range(ms * (USEC_PER_MSEC / 10), ms * USEC_PER_MSEC) with ms clamped to 1..10. Contract removed (it describes a function that sleeps and calls helper macros). Slice cut head; real function at 37-68.

name: vas_reconfig_capabilties
prose: Applies a DLPAR change of the credit count for VAS feature type to new_nr_creds. If type >= VAS_MAX_FEAT_TYPE it logs an error and returns -EINVAL without changing anything. Otherwise it takes vas_pseries_mutex, reads old_nr_creds from caps->nr_total_credits and stores new_nr_creds there. If old_nr_creds < new_nr_creds it calls reconfig_open_windows(vcaps, new_nr_creds - old_nr_creds, false); otherwise it computes nr_active_wins = nr_open_windows - nr_close_wins and, only if that exceeds new_nr_creds, calls reconfig_close_windows(vcaps, nr_active_wins - new_nr_creds, false). It releases the mutex and returns rc, which is 0 when no helper was called, or else the value returned by the helper that was called.
note: Reviewers concerned the old formal contract (removed). Prose rechecked at vas.c:851-900; rc is whatever the open/close helper returns, not necessarily negative errno only. Slice cut head.

name: vas_migration_handler
prose: Handles an LPM migration event action (intended VAS_SUSPEND or VAS_RESUME). It logs the event, and if copypaste_feat is false it returns 0 without touching migration_in_progress. Otherwise it sets migration_in_progress to true when action == VAS_SUSPEND and false for every other value, then loops over every feature type. Per feature it reads old_nr_creds, calls h_query_vas_capabilities (on success it takes new_nr_creds from target_lpar_creds and logs a mismatch if different; on failure it logs, and if action == VAS_RESUME it jumps to out returning that query error, otherwise it continues). Then in a switch on action: VAS_SUSPEND takes vas_pseries_mutex, calls reconfig_close_windows(vcaps, nr_open_windows, true), and waits (dropping the mutex and msleep(10)) while nr_open_wins_progress is nonzero, then releases the mutex (its rc is overwritten by the next iteration so a suspend-time error is ignored unless it is the last feature); VAS_RESUME takes the mutex, stores new_nr_creds in nr_total_credits, calls reconfig_open_windows(vcaps, new_nr_creds, true), and a nonzero rc jumps to out; any other action hits default, logs, sets rc = -EINVAL and jumps to out (after the first feature's query). If the loop completes it logs success. It returns rc: the value left by the last feature (0 on a successful resume; the last close_windows result on suspend), or the failing value from the paths above.
note: Reviewer 1 (suspend query failure does not return negative) right. Reviewer 15 (no invalid-action check; non-suspend takes resume path) WRONG: vas.c:1056-1060 default case returns -EINVAL (though migration_in_progress is already cleared for any non-suspend action at 989-992). Slice cut head; real function at 974-1074.

name: fsl_open_outb_mbox
prose: Opens the MPC85xx RapidIO outbound mailbox. It returns -EINVAL if entries is below RIO_MIN_TX_RING_SIZE, above RIO_MAX_TX_RING_SIZE or not a power of two. Otherwise it stores dev_id and size = entries in rmu->msg_tx_ring and, for each entry, allocates a RIO_MSG_BUFFER_SIZE coherent buffer with dma_alloc_coherent (GFP_KERNEL). If one allocation fails it sets rc = -ENOMEM and frees only those buffer slots that are non-NULL (the loop at fsl_rmu.c:742 checks each virt_buffer[j] before freeing), then returns -ENOMEM; the freed pointers are not cleared. Next it allocates the descriptor ring (size * RIO_MSG_DESC_SIZE, coherent); on failure it goes to out_dma, which frees all size message buffers unconditionally (they have all been allocated by then) and returns -ENOMEM. Then it sets tx_slot = 0, writes the ring physical address to odqdpar and odqepar, writes osar and osr, and calls request_irq for IRQ_RIO_TX(mport) with fsl_rio_tx_handler; if that returns a negative value it frees the descriptor ring at out_irq, falls through to out_dma (freeing all buffers) and returns that error. On success it programs omr (configuration, entry-count field from get_bitmask_order(entries) - 2, then the enable bit) and returns 0, keeping the allocations.
note: Reviewer 15 (out_dma frees all buffers on partial failure) WRONG for the buffer-allocation loop: fsl_rmu.c:742-750 guards each free with a NULL check and exits via goto out, not out_dma. out_dma (reached only after all buffers exist) frees every entry as the reviewer says, which is correct there. Slice cut head; real function at 719-813.

name: tsi108_eth_of_init
prose: Arch initcall that registers a tsi-ethernet platform device for each node compatible with tsi108-ethernet of type network. For each node it zeroes r[] and tsi_eth_data, reads the first address resource into r[0] (failure: goto err), builds an IRQ resource r[1], and registers a platform device with platform_device_register_simple("tsi-ethernet", i++, &r[0], 1) (only the address resource is passed; r[1] is not). If registration returns an error it goes to err with that error. It then reads the MAC address, dereferences the "mdio-handle" and "phy-handle" properties without NULL checks, finds the mdio node and reads its address resource (failure: unregister the device and goto err), finds the phy node (NULL gives -ENODEV via unreg), reads its "reg" value without a NULL check, fills regs, phyregs, phy and irq_num in tsi_eth_data, sets phy_type to TSI108_PHY_BCM54XX if txc-rxc-delay-disable is present, drops the phy node reference, and calls platform_device_add_data (failure: goto unreg). After all nodes it returns 0. The unreg label unregisters the current platform device and falls through to err, which calls of_node_put(np) and returns ret, so devices registered for earlier nodes stay registered on failure.
note: Reviewer 2 (only the address resource is registered) right. Reviewer 15 (success path never calls of_node_put(np)) WRONG: for_each_compatible_node drops the reference when it advances and ends with np NULL; of_node_put(np) at err is needed only because the goto leaves the loop early (tsi108_dev.c:148-151). Slice cut head; real function at 63-151.

name: icp_opal_init
prose: Init function. It looks up a device node compatible with ibm,opal-intc; if none exists it returns -ENODEV and leaves icp_ops unchanged. Otherwise it sets the global icp_ops to &icp_opal_ops, prints a banner with printk, releases the node with of_node_put and returns 0. These are the only two return paths.

name: insert_sh6
prose: Inserts the SH6 operand of the rld* instructions into insn and returns the result. It only ORs bits into insn and never clears any. If PPC_OP(insn) == 4 it ORs (value & 0x1f) << 6 (bits 6-10) and (value & 0x20) >> 5 (bit 0). Otherwise it ORs (value & 0x1f) << 11 (bits 11-15) and (value & 0x20) >> 4 (bit 1). The dialect and errmsg parameters are unused; *errmsg is not written and no error is reported.
note: Reviewer 15 (else branch sets bit 1, not bit 4) RIGHT: ppc-opc.c:1970 uses (value & 0x20) >> 4, which places value bit 5 at bit 1. Slice cut head; real function at 1960-1971.

name: memex
prose: xmon 'm' (memory examine) command; it has no parameters and returns void. It reads an address into adrs with scanhex, then looks at the next non-blank character: if it is '?' it prints memex_help_string and returns; otherwise it stores that character in termch. It then sets last_cmd = "m\n" (these two assignments happen once, before the loops, and are not updated later). It reads the rest of the line, treating 'b','w','l','d' as setting size to 1, 2, 4, 8, 'r' as toggling brev, 'n' as setting mnoread and '.' as clearing it, and clamps size to 1..8. It then enters an endless loop that prints adrs and the memory contents (read with mread unless mnoread is set, byte-reversed when brev), then reads sub-commands from the input line: a hex number is written to adrs with mwrite; other characters adjust adrs, size, mnoread or brev (for example ',' '^' '/' '\\' 'm' '<' '>' '\'' for strings, '?' to print memex_subcmd_help_string); a newline ends the inner loop and adrs advances by inc. The function returns only when the sub-command character is 'x' or EOF, after calling scannl() to consume the line.
note: Reviewer 15 (termch and last_cmd set once before the loop, not updated) RIGHT: xmon.c:2404-2406. Slice cut head and name; real function at 2391-2539.

name: kernel_vector_end
prose: Ends a kernel-mode vector region started with kernel_vector_begin(). If neither has_vector() nor has_xtheadvector() is true it triggers WARN_ON and returns without any other action. Otherwise it calls riscv_v_disable() and then riscv_v_stop_kernel_context(). In the CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_V_PREEMPTIVE build that helper returns 1 when riscv_v_ctx_get_depth() != 0 or no preemptible vector context has started for current (nothing else done), and otherwise clears the dirty flag, calls riscv_v_stop(RISCV_PREEMPT_V) and returns 0; in the non-preemptive build it is defined as the constant -ENOENT, which is nonzero. If the helper's result is nonzero, kernel_vector_end calls put_cpu_vector_context(), which calls riscv_v_stop(RISCV_KERNEL_MODE_V) and then local_bh_enable() (or preempt_enable() when CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT). If the result is 0 it does not call put_cpu_vector_context. The function does not itself restore any vector register state.
note: Reviewer 1 (restoration not done here) right; reviewer 2 (nonzero also when depth != 0) right; reviewer 15 (non-preemptive build uses -ENOENT) right: kernel_mode_vector.c:114-122,190-192. Code at 237-246. Slice cut head.
